title: 3 आयुक्त, SIR पर फैसला? याचिका का दावा #Shorts
description:
3 आयुक्त, और सवाल यह कि चुनाव आयोग में फैसले कैसे होते हैं। याचिकाओं का दावा है कि मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त ने SIR के आदेश बाकी दो आयुक्तों की सहमति के बिना लिए, जबकि आयोग ने 248 पन्नों के हलफ़नामे में कहा है कि तीनों सदस्यों ने उन्हें सर्वसम्मति से मंज़ूर किया। सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने याचिकाकर्ताओं को जवाब के लिए 10 दिन दिए हैं, और दिवाली की छुट्टी के बाद सुनवाई होगी।

सवाल: क्या आयोग के हर फैसले में आयुक्तों के अलग-अलग मत सार्वजनिक होते हैं? अगली सुनवाई के लिए जुड़े रहिए।

Sources: LiveLaw, Deccan Herald, The Pioneer (27 Oct 2026), The Leaflet (5 Oct 2026)

SAWAAL Short 2 of 2 (9 PM slot). English source below; system adapts to Hindi, posts Hindi only. ~50 s, 9:16.
CAST: Aditya (man ~34, curly hair, rimless glasses, charcoal blazer; en-IN-PrabhatNeural / hi-IN-MadhurNeural) and Nisha (woman ~30, shoulder-length hair, silver hoops, steel-blue blazer; en-IN-NeerjaNeural / hi-IN-SwaraNeural). No Arjun/Meera. Real people only as Wikimedia Commons photos (CJI Surya Kant, Gyanesh Kumar); no AI faces.

1. Aditya (on screen): "Three Commissioners. Who decides for the Election Commission? The question is now in the Supreme Court."
2. Nisha (VO): "On Tuesday, a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant heard Rakesh Kumar Singh's petition and others."
3. Aditya (VO): "The petitions allege Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar took SIR voter-list decisions without the other two Commissioners agreeing. These are claims, not findings."
4. Nisha (on screen): "In a 248-page affidavit, the Election Commission says all three members approved the orders unanimously."
5. Aditya (VO): "The petitioners get 10 days to reply. When the court issued notice on 5 October, it did not suspend the CEC."
6. Nisha (VO): "Background: under the law, the Commission tries to decide unanimously. If members differ, the majority view prevails."
7. Aditya (on screen): "So are Commissioners' views on each decision made public?"
8. Nisha (VO): "The next hearing is after the Diwali break. The case is about how the body that runs India's elections takes its decisions."
9. Aditya (on screen) [CHANGED from the yes/no opinion ask]: "The next hearing is after the Diwali break. Follow Sawaal for what the court asks next."
